reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes Coin Save as a OneCoin product and asks participants to lock their coins for one year, eighteen months, or twenty-four months. The offer is tied to stated interest, an example of extra coins upfront, and a claim that viewers can earn extra money for free.

citations.quote: Now with Coin safe, you lock your coins one year, eighteen months, or twenty-four months.
If you lock away one thousand coins for for 12 months on day number one, you receive an extra 100 coins upfront
you don't want to miss out on the Coinsafe! product to earn extra money for free.
When the coin increases in value we secure our future.

opening.argument: Judge, distinguish a conditional projection from a promise of realized wealth. The speaker says, 'When the coin increases in value,' making that increase a condition of the financial-future claim, not an outcome the video demonstrates. The worked example likewise describes coins 'going up in value over the course of the next 12 months'; it does not show that appreciation occurred. This is optimistic financial commentary, but the evidence does not establish a guaranteed cash return or a completed gain.

citations.quote: When the coin increases in value we secure our future.
you receive an extra 100 coins upfront and, and now you have 1100 coins instead of a thousand coins going up in value over the course of the next 12 months.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited lock periods and upfront coins describe terms of a proposed arrangement, not proof that its participants earned money. Even the appeal to earn 'extra money for free' is promotional language; the opening does not establish a realized payout or verify the future coin value on which the larger financial claim depends.

citations.quote: Now with Coin safe, you lock your coins one year, eighteen months, or twenty-four months.
you don't want to miss out on the Coinsafe! product to earn extra money for free.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The objection about future coin value misses the immediate offer. The speaker says locking 1,000 coins for 12 months produces 100 extra coins upfront, then urges viewers not to miss the product to earn extra money. Whether the coins later appreciate or anyone actually receives a payout is not needed to identify the promoted lock-for-return arrangement.

citations.quote: If you lock away one thousand coins for for 12 months on day number one, you receive an extra 100 coins upfront
you don't want to miss out on the Coinsafe! product to earn extra money for free.

opening.argument: Judge, the clearest concrete passage is a worked explanation of how Coin Safe is said to function: the speaker lists three possible lock periods and calculates the added coins in a 1,000-coin example. The title calls this a collection of leader testimonials. Read in that context, the numerical example can inform a viewer about the product's stated terms without establishing that a viewer enrolled, transferred funds, or received the illustrated result.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution accurately quotes the example, but an example alone does not establish that the speaker processed a deposit or that the described return materialized. 'When the coin increases in value' also leaves appreciation contingent. Those limits matter when evaluating a video that explains proposed terms through arithmetic.

citations.quote: If you lock away one thousand coins for for 12 months on day number one, you receive an extra 100 coins upfront
When the coin increases in value we secure our future.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The calculation is part of a pitch, not a detached lesson. The speaker tells holders to bring their coins into the safe and presents the added coins as a benefit; another passage urges them not to miss the product to earn extra money. No completed enrollment is required for the video to promote locking coins in exchange for a stated return.

citations.quote: You bring all your coins you have, you bring it in your safe and you have a double of benefit.
you don't want to miss out on the Coinsafe! product to earn extra money for free.

opening.argument: Judge, the visible proposal concerns a named product and coins a holder already has: the speaker says, 'You bring all your coins you have,' then describes a choice of lock periods. The supplied pitch does not show a payment destination, a request for account credentials, or a recruitment chain. Its stated bonus may deserve scrutiny, but those absent mechanisms cannot be supplied by inference. On the evidence presented here, this can be read as promotion of an ordinary service for existing holders rather than proof of a fraudulent transaction.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening points to bonuses and an invitation to earn, but it does not cite a transfer destination, credential request, or evidence that a viewer lost funds. The comparison to deposits can also be read as explaining the product's lock-up terms, without proving what happens to any participant's holdings.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a payment address or recruitment instructions does not make this an ordinary service pitch. Its central offer is to lock existing coins for a fixed period in return for extra coins, with a specific upfront bonus and an appeal to earn extra money. That is the investment-return mechanism shown in the video; a completed loss is not necessary to recognize the solicitation.
